q: The expensive mistake in Python is
options: Writing a function that already exists, worse
why: Which is why the reflex worth building is asking "has somebody solved this" before typing.

q: A regular expression is the wrong tool for
options: Anything nested: HTML, JSON, source code
why: It has no memory of how deep it is, so every attempt works on your examples and fails on somebody else's.

why: Store and compute in UTC with aware objects; convert at the edges with `zoneinfo`.

q: For tokens, passwords and keys, use
options: `secrets`, which draws from the operating system's cryptographic source
why: `random` is a Mersenne Twister: a few outputs are enough to recover the state and predict the rest.

q: Building a URL by concatenating values
options: Lets a value containing `&` or a space become part of the URL's structure
Is fine if the values are validated
why: The same principle as SQL, shell commands and HTML: concatenation hopes the values contain nothing meaningful.

why: Wrong when the program is a script whose output is the point.

Is deprecated in favour of SQLAlchemy

options: `pandas` has fifteen years of answers written down; `polars` is faster with a more consistent API
why: On a new project handling real volume, `polars`. When you need an answer that already exists, `pandas`.

q: The number of dependencies that matters is
options: The transitive one, because each brings its own release schedule and advisories
why: You discover this the first time two of them disagree about a third.

q: Write it yourself rather than take a dependency when
options: The whole problem fits in your head
why: A retry loop fits. A timezone database does not.

q: When evaluating a package, read the issue tracker because
options: The tutorial says what it does well and the issues say what it does badly
It shows how active the project is
It is faster than the docs
why: Sort by most commented. You need both halves to decide whether it fits.

why: Its tables, progress bars and tracebacks are for a person looking at a terminal.
